name: libpng
notes: windows: shared-pass (upgraded from static-pass) -- root-caused and fixed for real, not worked around. Four independent, genuine bugs found and fixed in order:

1. libtool's own cygwin*/mingw* archive_cmds are gated behind a literal `$LD --help 2>&1 | grep 'auto-import'` probe. tools/crt-cc's real linker backend (confirmed via `crt-cc -shared -v`) is `ld.lld -m i386pep`/`-m arm64pe` -- a genuine, capable GNU/MinGW-compatible personality that DOES support --enable-auto-import (verified directly: `ld.lld -m i386pep --help` lists it) -- but a bare `$LD --help` (no -m flag) falls back to ld.lld's generic ELF frontend, which doesn't. Fixed at the root in tools/crt-native-tool: when the wrapped tool is ld.lld (matched case-insensitively, handling both the real filename and the NTFS 8.3 short-path alias tools/crt-port-build.py's windows_short_path() substitutes, e.g. LDLLD~1.EXE), always inject the right -m emulation up front -- so every direct $LD invocation (not just the ones tools/crt-cc itself drives) sees exactly the same real, capable personality. This made `checking whether ... supports shared libraries`/`checking if libtool supports shared libraries` resolve yes for the first time.

2. libtool always compiles a second, -DPIC -DDLL_EXPORT pass for the shared variant. pngpriv.h's own, upstream-documented mechanism (`#ifdef DLL_EXPORT -> PNG_BUILD_DLL -> PNG_IMPEXP=PNG_DLL_EXPORT`) then needed PNG_DLL_EXPORT/PNG_DLL_IMPORT, which pngconf.h only defines inside its own `#if defined(_WIN32) || ... || defined(__CYGWIN__)` block -- exactly what this recipe's CFLAGS deliberately undefine (to keep libpng off the `#include <windows.h>` path this sysroot doesn't have). Fixed via the command-line override pngpriv.h itself documents as sanctioned ("the builder of the library may set this on the command line"): added `-DPNG_DLL_EXPORT=__declspec(dllexport) -DPNG_DLL_IMPORT=__declspec(dllimport)` to this recipe's Windows CFLAGS.

3. libtool's own generated wrapper source for uninstalled test/contrib executables (`.libs/lt-*.c`, generated by ltmain.sh itself, not part of libpng) unconditionally `#include <malloc.h>` -- this sysroot never had one. Added include/malloc.h following Android Bionic's own convention exactly (bionic/libc/include/malloc.h): a thin compatibility header that just re-exports <stdlib.h>'s malloc family for source compatibility with pre-POSIX code; deliberately declares no allocator-extension symbols (malloc_usable_size(), memalign(), ...) since this libc doesn't implement them yet.

4. Even with the linker-family detection fixed, libtool separately refused to link libpng16 as a DLL against zlib's already-built shared library, because its own dependent-library file-magic check (`deplibs_check_method='file_magic file format (pei*-i386(.*architecture: i386)?|pe-arm-wince|pe-x86-64|pe-aarch64)'`, `file_magic_cmd='$OBJDUMP -f'`) never matches: `llvm-objdump -f` reports `file format coff-x86-64` for this project's own real .so/.dll files, not GNU objdump's `pe-x86-64` the hardcoded regex expects -- a genuine LLVM-vs-GNU-binutils output-format naming difference, not a real problem with the library file itself. Since the regex lives inside the generated `configure`/`libtool` scripts (not something a recipe CFLAGS override can reach), fixed the standard, portable way real cross-toolchain builds already use for exactly this situation: set `lt_cv_deplibs_check_method=pass_all` as an environment variable (autoconf's `${VAR+set}` cache-variable idiom honors a pre-set env var and skips its own detection entirely, the same mechanism $LD/$DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP already rely on elsewhere in this project). UPDATE: since this is a fixed, permanent fact about this toolchain (not libpng-specific at all -- any future Windows configure recipe going through GNU Libtool with a shared-library dependency would hit the identical mismatch), generalized into tools/crt-port-build.py's make_env() itself (alongside the $LD/$DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP defaults) while investigating libffi's own shared-library build -- this recipe's own explicit setting is now redundant (same value either way) but left in place as self-documenting history.

5. Separately (build-time, not configure-time): `libtool: syntax error: unexpected '|'` from libtool's generated `nm ... |  | sed ...` pipeline -- config.log showed `NM='nm'`, i.e. never resolved past the literal default, so `checking command to parse ... nm output` failed and left `$global_symbol_pipe` empty, producing a pipeline with nothing between two pipes. Root cause: unlike $LD/$DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP, tools/crt-port-build.py's make_env() never preset $NM to a real tool at all. Fixed the same way as those three: preset $NM to llvm-nm.exe (via find_windows_host_tool()) and added NM to the crt-native-tool wrapping loop. Verified: `checking command to parse ... nm output... ok`; full rebuild's syntax-error count dropped to 0; ctest 79/79.

7. Also found and fixed (cosmetic, not build-blocking, but a genuine correctness bug in the generated `.libs/lt-*.c` wrappers): every `make`/`make install` run printed repeated non-fatal `libtool: error: Could not determine host file/path name ... Continuing, but uninstalled executables may not work.` warnings for every contrib/libtests helper linked against the uninstalled shared libpng16. Root-caused, not just silenced: configure's own logic picks the build-to-host path-conversion function via `case $host in *-*-mingw* ) case $build in *-*-mingw*|*-*-windows* ) # actually msys -> lt_cv_to_host_file_cmd=func_convert_file_msys_to_w32`. Autoconf's authors used '$build also looks like mingw/windows' purely as a historical proxy for 'configure is running inside a real MSYS2 shell' -- true for every toolchain they anticipated, but not for this project's own from-scratch mksh/toybox PAL, which is a genuinely native $build with no MSYS/Cygwin runtime underneath. `func_convert_file_msys_to_w32`'s real implementation shells out to a literal `cmd //c echo ...`, relying on real MSYS's own automatic POSIX-argv-to-Windows-path translation (a feature of msys-2.0.dll's exec() layer, not of cmd.exe itself) -- but this project's rootfs $PATH is deliberately scoped to just its own sysroot bin dirs, so `cmd` is never found, the conversion always returns empty, and libtool falls back to its own documented 'deliberately simplistic' recovery: a blind `s/:/;/g` on the *original* string -- which corrupts every path this project uses (`C:/Users/...`), since the drive-letter colon isn't a path-list separator the way a real POSIX build's colons would be. Confirmed directly: a real generated wrapper's `LIB_PATH_VALUE` had become `"C;/Users/..."`. Fixed the same standard way as bug 4 above: `lt_cv_to_host_file_cmd` and its sibling `lt_cv_to_tool_file_cmd` are both autoconf cache variables (the `${VAR+y}` idiom skips detection when pre-set); preset both to `func_convert_file_noop` -- libtool's own built-in 'paths are already in host format, nothing to convert' case (the exact value a real non-mingw/non-cygwin host already gets in that same case statement's 'otherwise' branch), which is precisely correct here since this project's paths were never MSYS/POSIX-style to begin with. `to_host_path_cmd` has no cache variable of its own -- it's derived at runtime from `to_host_file_cmd` by libtool's own `func_init_to_host_path_cmd`, so fixing the file variant fixes the path variant too. Generalized directly into `tools/crt-port-build.py`'s `make_env()` (alongside `lt_cv_deplibs_check_method`), not left recipe-local, since it's a fixed, permanent fact about this toolchain, true for any Windows configure-based recipe going through GNU Libtool. Does NOT touch `$host` classification or any DLL/EXE/import-lib generation logic (a separate, outer `case $host in *-*-mingw* )` decision) -- confirmed the shared-build chain (bugs 1-5 above) is completely unaffected. Verified: warning count 0 (was ~27 per full rebuild); re-inspected a real generated wrapper's `LIB_PATH_VALUE`, now correctly `"C:/Users/.../.libs:"` (drive letter intact); ran the freshly-built `pnggetset.exe` (a wrapper whose `EXE_PATH_VALUE` has 3 colon-joined directory entries, the most exercised case) directly -- all 6 of its PLTE/hIST/tRNS/tEXt/sPLT/unknown-chunks get-then-set roundtrip subtests PASS, rc=0. (Residual, deliberately not chased further: the resulting `LIB_PATH_VALUE`/`EXE_PATH_VALUE` strings stay `:`-joined rather than the `;` a literal Windows `PATH` env var expects for multi-entry values -- but this recipe's own `-U_WIN32` CFLAGS also makes the wrapper's own `IS_PATH_SEPARATOR` macro fall back to recognizing only `:` (its `PATH_SEPARATOR_2 = ';'` definition is gated behind `#if defined _WIN32 ...`, deliberately undefined here), so this is self-consistent within this project's own convention, and empirically caused no failure in either the single-entry or 3-entry case actually tested -- attributed to Windows' own 'search the executable's own directory first' default DLL resolution already finding the co-located `.libs/*.dll` regardless of what this PATH-prepending mechanism contributes).

End-to-end verified, not just 'it built': a standalone test program (crt-cc, linked against the installed libpng16.dll.a import lib + libz) dynamically loaded the real libpng16-16.dll and successfully called png_access_version_number()/png_get_header_ver() (both returned the correct 1.6.57), then did a real png_create_write_struct()/png_create_info_struct()/png_destroy_write_struct() round trip through the DLL. Full ctest stayed at 79/79 throughout every step of this chain (crt-native-tool is used by every Windows configure-recipe build, so this was the highest-stakes regression check).

NOW FIXED (was previously listed here as a known, not-yet-fixed issue): every libtool-generated `.libs/lt-*.c` uninstalled-execution wrapper (pngtest, pngcp, png-fix-itxt, and the contrib/libtests helpers) hit `_getcwd`/`_stat`/`struct _stat`/`_chmod`/`_putenv`/`_setmode`/`_spawnv`/`_P_WAIT` as undeclared. Root cause: ltmain.sh's wrapper template has two *independent*, mismatched conditionals -- an `#if defined _WIN32 && !defined __GNUC__` that correctly picks <unistd.h> once this recipe's CFLAGS undefine _WIN32, but a separate `#elif defined __MINGW32__` macro-rename block (getcwd->_getcwd, stat->_stat, etc.) that fires regardless, since __MINGW32__ stays defined. Fixed with a new project-owned shim, porting/shims/win32/libtool_wrapper_compat.h: real posix_spawn()-based _spawnv()/_P_WAIT and a no-op _setmode() (this PAL's I/O is already byte-transparent, no CRLF mode to switch), plus #define _getcwd getcwd (and _stat/_chmod/_putenv) which cancels out against the wrapper's own later #define getcwd _getcwd via the C preprocessor's 'blue paint' self-reference rule -- whichever spelling ends up in the wrapper body resolves back to this project's real Bionic-style POSIX name either way. Wired in via a new `force_include` recipe field (tools/crt-port-build.py's apply_recipe_env()), which folds `-include <shim>` into **CFLAGS**, not CPPFLAGS: Automake's implicit compile rule reads both CPPFLAGS and CFLAGS, but its LINK rule (`$(CCLD) $(AM_CFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) $(AM_LDFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ ...`) never references CPPFLAGS at all -- and that LINK line is exactly where libtool generates *and* compiles a `.libs/lt-*.c` wrapper in one step when linking an executable against an uninstalled shared library. A first attempt that put the -include flag in CPPFLAGS compiled fine for ordinary library sources (png.c, pngerror.c, ...) but silently never reached the wrapper compiles at all -- confirmed directly by diffing the real build log's pngtest.o compile line (had -include, via CPPFLAGS) against its pngtest.exe link line (missing -include entirely, since LINK doesn't read CPPFLAGS). End-to-end verified, not just compiled: the built pngtest.exe (top-level libtool wrapper, exercising the shim's _spawnv()/_getcwd()/etc. at actual runtime, not just compile time) was run directly and printed libpng's full self-test output ending in 'libpng passes test', rc=0. pngtest.exe and pngcp.exe both now build and install successfully. Full ctest stayed at 79/79.

Also found, real but session-local (not a code bug): `make install`'s libtool-generated `install-header-links`/`install-exec-hook` steps (`rm -f X; ln -s Y X` for each top-level header/lib alias, e.g. png.h -> libpng16/png.h) intermittently fail with `ln: ... File exists` on a REBUILD when X was already a valid symlink from a prior successful install -- reproducible across repeated reruns in this session, but an isolated, minimal `rm -f <symlink>; ln -s` repro via the exact same rootfs mksh + toybox rm succeeded cleanly, so this looks like Windows delete-pending/handle-timing noise from repeated same-session rebuilds rather than a general toybox/CRT rm-on-symlink bug -- worth a closer look if it reproduces from a genuinely cold `out/` directory.
Requires zlib installed into PORT_PREFIX first.

linux/macos: shared-pass -- unlike Windows (blocked by GNU Libtool's MinGW/lld-link shared-library detection, see the windows note below), libpng's real GNU Libtool build produces a working shared library on both Linux and macOS through this project's real system ld/ld64. Confirmed via ldd on a real Linux aarch64 machine: libpng16.so.16.57.0's libz.so.1 dependency resolves to this project's own port-tests/install/lib/libz.so.1, not the host's system zlib package -- fixed by adding -Wl,-rpath,<PORT_PREFIX>/lib to shared_mode's macOS/Linux link flags in tools/crt-port-build.py's make_env(), so one port's shared library can find a sibling port's shared library, not just this project's own sysroot libc/libm/libdl/libc++. macOS confirmed via the same generic rpath fix plus the user's own report that the shared library builds cleanly there.
The first successful CRT configure run required vfprintf, sprintf, vsprintf, inttypes.h, strings.h, strtoimax, strtoumax, bzero, and bcmp.

libpng's configure is real GNU Autoconf output (unlike zlib's hand-written script), so it runs config.guess, which does not recognize plain Windows `uname` output (`uname -s = Windows`, no MSYS/Cygwin/MinGW userland) and fails with 'unable to guess system type'. --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@ works around this; the placeholder is resolved by tools/crt-port-build.py's own arch detection (--target-arch flag, else CRT_TARGET_ARCH env var, else platform.machine()) to aarch64-w64-mingw32 or x86_64-w64-mingw32, so this recipe works unmodified on both Windows architectures.

target_overrides.windows.env has the same -U_WIN32/-U__WIN32__/etc. CFLAGS trick as zlib.json, plus -U__NT__ (pngpriv.h's own Windows guard also checks __NT__): without it, pngpriv.h's `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__WIN32__) || defined(__NT__) / #include <windows.h>` fires -- this project's sysroot has no real Windows SDK <windows.h> (its own Win32 API surface is declared privately inside libc/src/arch/windows/, not exposed publicly) -- and configure fails outright with 'windows.h file not found'. Nothing near that include in pngpriv.h/png.c/pngerror.c actually references a real Windows API symbol from it, so undefining the trigger macros (keeping libpng on its generic/POSIX code paths, matching what this project's CRT actually provides) is correct, not just a workaround -- same reasoning as zlib.json's own note. Scoped to Windows only since these macros are never predefined on macOS/Linux anyway; an earlier version of this recipe applied both this and --build=aarch64-w64-mingw32 unconditionally, which broke the macOS build (libtool concluded the target was MinGW/Windows and tried to invoke an MSVC-style `lib -OUT:...` archiver step that does not exist on macOS).

SUPERSEDED by the shared-pass root-cause fix chain recorded at the top of this notes array -- kept only as the historical trail of the original investigation. windows: static-pass, shared attempted and root-caused but NOT achieved -- unlike zlib (a hand-written Makefile that calls tools/crt-cc -shared directly, which this project's crt-cc/crt-c++ now fully support), libpng's build goes through real GNU Libtool, whose MinGW shared-library machinery is hardcoded around a classic GNU-binutils toolchain. First pass: config.log showed `checking for dlltool` / `checking for objdump` both resolving to false (this project ships LLVM's own llvm-dlltool/llvm-objdump, not binaries literally named dlltool/objdump) and `checking if the linker is GNU ld` resolving to yes even though the actual linker is lld-link.exe in its MSVC-compatible mode (misdetected because --target=*-w64-mingw32 makes clang report a GNU-flavored linker frontend). tools/crt-port-build.py's make_env() was extended to pre-set $DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP to llvm-dlltool/llvm-objdump (same technique already used for $LD -- see that env-var's own comment in make_env()), and a rebuild confirmed both probes now resolve correctly (`checking for dlltool... .../llvm-dlltool.exe`, `checking for objdump... .../llvm-objdump.exe`) -- but `checking whether the ... linker ... supports shared libraries` still resolves to no, and libpng16.so is still not produced. This later check runs as one continuous block of libtool-internal shell logic (configure script lines ~10962 to ~12246 with no compiler/linker invocation logged in between), i.e. a static host_os/with_gnu_ld-driven case-statement decision, not an actual failed compile probe -- meaning something else in that decision tree (plausibly stemming from the incorrect with_gnu_ld=yes verdict steering libtool toward MinGW+real-GNU-ld archive_cmds that assume flag syntax e.g. -Wl,--out-implib=... that crt-cc's actual lld-link /DLL linking does not speak) still rejects this toolchain. Not narrowed further; teaching libtool a working custom linker 'tag' for this toolchain (or getting it to correctly detect lld-link as non-GNU, matching the intended `*GNU ld*`-style pattern that a plain `LLD ... (compatible with GNU linkers)` -v banner should NOT match but evidently does against whatever pattern this libtool.m4 vintage actually uses) is a materially bigger undertaking than the zlib case and is left as a known, documented limitation. The $DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP env wiring itself is kept regardless -- it's a real, harmless, and independently correct improvement to make_env() (matching real tool availability) even though it wasn't sufficient on its own here.

windows: also observed (non-fatal) libtool warnings during `make` for several contrib/tools and contrib/libtests helper executables ('libtool: error: Could not determine host file name corresponding to .libs/'), a path-translation quirk in libtool's own relink step unrelated to the shared-library question above; libtool falls back to linking those helper .exe files directly against the static libpng16.a and every one of them still built successfully.
